next_step: Finalize Dedicated pricing and run 1M doc nightly indexing POC
notes:
— Summary: mid-market SaaS (product analytics) evaluating Redwood for embeddings + semantic search. Primary goal: reduce search latency at scale and replace brittle ES-based semantic layer.

— Timeline / recent activity:
  • 2025-11-18: inbound MQL from CTO; initial discovery (Maya).
  • 2025-12-05: architecture deep-dive w/ SE (Diego) — provided traffic patterns and nightly batch sizes.
  • 2026-01-22: Hosted API demo (embedding + vector search) — good first pass; liked Redwood streaming + function calling.
  • 2026-02-15: Proof-of-concept started: Hosted API + Pinecone connector; running synthetic workloads.
  • 2026-02-27: Live demo recording (ff_20260227_np-demo-1).
  • 2026-03-02: Dedicated pricing intro call; asked for 99%ile latency SLOs and reserved throughput pricing.
  • 2026-03-09: Integration test — bulk ingest 250k docs, indexing pipeline time ~3.5h (target <6h).

— POC requirements & metrics (customer-specified):
  • Workload: nightly batch ingestion ~1M documents (mix of product docs + user transcripts).
  • Embedding dim: 1536 (customer uses open embeddings today; evaluating switching).
  • Vector DB: currently Pinecone in prod; testing Milvus for cost; want Redwood to integrate cleanly (connectors + maintenance ops).
  • Throughput target: 200 QPS retrieval requests during business hours for semantic search API (peak bursts to 500 QPS).
  • Latency target: end-to-end retrieval + soft rerank 95th <= 150ms; prefer 100ms if possible.
  • Batch SLA: nightly full-index window must complete within maintenance window (2–6am PST).
  • Cost sensitivity: aims to reduce per-query cost by 30% vs current managed vector + CPU rerank stack.

— Tech preferences & constraints:
  • Prefer hosted API to validate latency/cost profile quickly, then migrate to Dedicated if throughput/latency/segregation justify.
  • Require VPC peering and KMS integration for Dedicated.
  • Data residency: primary tenant data must remain in US regions; legal requires addendum.
  • SSO: Okta SAML required for Console access.

— Notes from calls (shorthand / quotes):
  • "We need predictable costs for nightly indexing — spikes kill our forecasts." — Head of Ops.
  • "If Dedicated drops unit cost and keeps p95 under 120ms, it's a no-brainer." — VP Product.
  • SE comment: "Indexing throughput looks good but need batching recommendations and KV cache for chat flows."

— Integration & testing status:
  • Pinecone connector: basic read/write tests passed; need vector upsert rate benchmarking.
  • Milvus PoC: initial tests show lower storage costs but higher ops overhead. Customer wants Redwood to support both in Dedicated runbook.
  • Embedding pipeline: currently CPU-bound; investigating Redwood Optimize suggestions (quantization + batching).

— Commercial / procurement:
  • Topline: mid-market ARR expectation $50k–$150k. Procurement timeline targeted for 2026-04.
  • Pricing ask: reserved throughput tiers w/ burst credits + predictable nightly batch pricing.
  • Blockers: legal/data residency clause, SOC2 evidence, internal budget sign-off in April.

— Next actions (short):
  1) Deliver Dedicated pricing worksheet + usage model by 2026-03-17 (Maya + Diego).
  2) Run 1M doc nightly indexing test on Hosted (staged) and report timings (SE team).
  3) Provide SOC2 artifacts & KMS integration guide (share Drive link).
  4) Schedule exec pricing review with finance (VP Product + Redwood AE).

— Misc: Customer open to a 6–12 month reserved commit if SLA + pricing meet targets. High likelihood to move to Dedicated after POC.
